summary: Bronislaw Malinowski studied at Jagiellonian University, Leipzig, and the London School of Economics under Charles Gabriel Seligman. He held posts at the London School of Economics (~1922–1938), Cornell University (~1933), and Yale University (~1939–1942).

Bronwyn Finnigan works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. She studied at the Universities of Auckland, Sydney, and Melbourne. She held posts at the University of Auckland (~2008–2012), Marquette University (2012–2014), and the Australian National University (2014).

Brook Ziporyn specializes in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Chicago and the University of Michigan under Donald J. Munro. He held posts at Northwestern, the National University of Singapore, and the University of Chicago.
Brooke Schedneck is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Arizona State University under the supervision of Juliane Schober.

Bruce Charles Williams, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology, studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, Akira Fujieda, and Noritoshi Aramaki.

Bruce John Stewart, working in Buddhist studies and Indology, studied at Sakya College in 1978 and completed his PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman, also studying under Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Lincoln, working in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studied at Haverford and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade. He held academic posts at the University of Minnesota (~1976–1995) and the University of Chicago (~1995–2020).

Bruce Matthews, a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar, completed graduate studies at McMaster University (~1968–1974). He held posts as a Commonwealth Fellow at the University of Ceylon (~1971–1973) and as Professor of Comparative Religion at Acadia University (~1976–2006).
Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies and Indology. He held academic posts at Columbia University (attested 1988) and Wheaton College as associate professor of anthropology (attested 2019).
Bruno Dagens, a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology, studied under Colette Caillat and served as a professor at KU Leuven from approximately 1977 to 1986.
Bruno Galasek, working in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earned his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied under Franz Kielhorn (~1884–1886). He later held posts at Heidelberg University (~1890–1921) and the University of Breslau, where he was Professor Ordinarius (attested 1902).

Bruno Lindner, a scholar in Indology and linguistics, studied as a pupil under Rudolf von Roth from approximately 1876 to 1878. He held an academic post at Leipzig University from approximately 1882 to 1923.

Bryan D. Lowe, working in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, studied at Otani University, with graduate advisor Jacqueline I. Stone and other teachers. He held a post at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017).

Bryan J. Cuevas, a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, earned degrees from Emory and the University of Virginia. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Princeton and served as John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State University.
Bryce Ryan held academic posts at the University of Ceylon and Cornell University, and he taught Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah.

Bulcsu Siklós, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, completed his PhD at the University of London under Tadeusz Skorupski and Charles R. Bawden. He was affiliated with SOAS University of London (attested 1996).
Bunkyo Aoki, a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies, was a disciple of Kozui Otani from approximately 1910 to 1917 and later held a post at the University of Tokyo.

Bunyiu Nanjio, an Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Oxford under Friedrich Max Müller and Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He held posts as Sanskrit Professor at the University of Tokyo (~1887–1906) and President of Otani University (~1914–1923).

Bunzaburo Matsumoto, a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, studied at the University of Tokyo (~1890–1893). He held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1899–1906) and Kyoto University (1906–1929; attested 1934).
